wind.definition: the natural movement of air outside; a breeze.
examples: The wind is strong today.

write.definition: to form letters or words on a surface with a pen or pencil; to compose text.
examples: She likes to write poems.

writer.definition: a person who writes; someone who composes text.
examples: The writer spoke about his book.

writing.definition: words that have been written down; the act of composing text.
examples: Her writing is clear and concise.

written.definition: produced or written in letters on paper or another surface.
examples: Please bring the written notes.

work.definition: activity involving mental or physical effort done to achieve a result.
examples: She enjoys her work.

worker.definition: a person who works; a laborer.
examples: The workers met the deadline.
The factory is working at full capacity.
A well worked plan.

water.definition: a clear liquid essential for most forms of life.
examples: Drink water every day.

wrench.definition: a tool used to grip and turn objects such as bolts.
examples: He used a wrench to loosen the pipe joint.

wry.definition: containing or showing a dry, especially mocking, humor.
examples: She gave a wry smile after the joke fell flat.
The meeting took a weird turn after the announcement.

west.definition: the direction to the left when you face north
examples: The mountains are west of the city.
Go west for three blocks.

west.definition: in or toward the west direction
examples: They bought a house in west London.
The plane flew west.

wistful.definition: feeling sad in a gentle way because you want something that is gone or difficult
examples: She became wistful when she talked about her childhood.
He had a wistful smile.

waifish.definition: very thin in a fragile-looking way
examples: The model had a waifish figure.
She looked waifish in the winter coat.

whirr.definition: a continuous soft sound like the spinning of a motor
examples: I heard a whirr from the fan.
The computer made a whirr.

whirr.definition: to make a continuous soft spinning sound
examples: The wheels whirred as the cart moved.
A motor whirred in the background.

watch.definition: a small device worn on the wrist to tell the time
examples: My watch is fast.
He checked his watch.

watch.definition: to look at something over a period of time
examples: We watched the movie together.
She watched the kids play.

weaver.definition: a person or machine that makes fabric by weaving threads
examples: The weaver created a beautiful scarf.
My grandmother was a weaver.

wander.definition: to walk or move around without a clear destination
examples: We wandered around the old town.
Don’t wander too far from the group.
The character sounded wrathful in the final scene.
A wrathful voice made everyone quiet.

wrath.definition: strong anger, especially when it lasts for a long time
examples: She left in wrath after the unfair decision.
The speech threatened the crowd with wrath.

waver.definition: to change your mind or become less certain; to hesitate
examples: He wavered before agreeing to the plan.
The candidate wavered when asked about his past work.

wayfarer.definition: a person traveling on foot, especially for a long distance
examples: The wayfarer asked for directions at the crossroads.
A lone wayfarer reached the town by nightfall.

whisper.definition: to speak very quietly, usually so that only a person nearby can hear
examples: She whispered his name into my ear.
Don’t whisper in class.

whisper.definition: soft speech or a quiet sound made by speaking quietly
examples: I heard a whisper behind me.
There was a whisper of wind through the trees.

warp.definition: to twist or change shape out of normal form, often slowly or due to heat or pressure
examples: The hot sun can warp plastic.
The wood warped after it got wet.

warp.definition: a distortion or change in shape, especially caused by heat or pressure
examples: There was a warp in the door frame.
The test showed a slight warp in the metal.

wane.definition: to gradually become less strong or less common
examples: Interest in the project began to wane.
The storm finally wane d at dawn.

wretched.definition: very unhappy, uncomfortable, or of poor quality
examples: He felt wretched after losing his wallet.
The hotel room was wretched and dirty.
Whence did the rumor begin?
She asked whence he had received the information.

whereby.definition: by means of which; in the way that leads to a result
examples: The guide explains how to submit the form, whereby you can receive confirmation.
She improved the system whereby errors were reduced.

whilst.definition: during the time that; at the same time as
examples: I read a book whilst waiting for the train.
She listened to music whilst studying.
The situation worsened after the argument.
His back pain worsened at night.

withhold.definition: to keep something back or not give it to someone
examples: She withheld the information until it was confirmed.
They withheld the report pending review.

withstand.definition: to resist something and not be harmed or affected by it
examples: The building is designed to withstand strong winds.
She withstood pressure from the other team.

wherein.definition: in which; in the place, part, or condition mentioned
examples: The document explains the rules wherein the plan applies.

whereas.definition: used to introduce a contrast or explanation, especially in legal or formal writing
examples: Whereas the defendant denies the claim, the evidence suggests otherwise.
The policy was updated, whereas the older version is now out of date.

watchful.definition: carefully observing to notice possible danger or problems
examples: The watchful guard noticed the suspicious activity.
Stay watchful when you cross the street.

wroughtiron.definition: iron that has been worked and shaped, often used for fences or decorative structures
examples: The railing was made of wrought iron.
They restored the wrought iron gate carefully.

wrinkle.definition: a small fold or line in skin or fabric
examples: There was a wrinkle on the back of his shirt.
She smoothed the wrinkle from the paper.

wrinkle.definition: to make small folds or lines, or to become folded and lined
examples: The heat wrinkled the plastic cover.
His forehead wrinkled when he read the form.

weathered.definition: changed by long exposure to weather, especially becoming rough or faded
examples: The house had a weathered wooden fence.
His face looked weathered by years of outdoor work.

wan.definition: looking pale and unhealthy, often because of illness, tiredness, or lack of light
examples: He felt tired and his face looked wan.
The light made her skin seem wan.

wisecrack.definition: a witty remark meant to be funny, often in response to something
examples: He made a wisecrack that made everyone laugh.
Her wisecrack ended the awkward silence.
He wisecracked during the interview.
They kept wisecracking to break the tension.

wary.definition: careful about possible danger or problems
examples: Be wary of emails that ask for passwords.
She was wary after her previous experience.

workable.definition: able to work in a practical situation
examples: The plan is workable, but we need more time.
We found a workable solution.

worth.definition: the value or importance of something
examples: The watch is worth a lot of money.
Her advice is worth listening to.

worth.definition: having the value or importance that makes it deserve attention
examples: It’s worth the effort.
That idea is worth considering.
Whither did they go?
Whither should we travel next?

wintry.definition: like winter, with cold weather or winter conditions
examples: A wintry storm moved through the region.
The forecast is wintry this week.

withdrawal.definition: the act of taking money from an account or getting it back
examples: There was a fee for each withdrawal from the ATM.
I made a withdrawal to pay for the trip.

withdrawal.definition: a move away from a place or from an activity
examples: The army began a withdrawal after the ceasefire.
Her withdrawal from the project surprised the team.

withdrawal.definition: health or mental symptoms that can happen when someone stops using a drug or alcohol
examples: The doctor warned him about withdrawal.
Withdrawal can start within a few hours after stopping.

weigh.definition: to determine how heavy something is
examples: Weigh the package before you ship it.
I weighed myself in the morning.

weigh.definition: to consider something carefully when making a decision
examples: She weighed the costs before accepting the job.
Weigh your options carefully.

warrant.definition: a legal document that gives official permission to do something, often to search
examples: Police need a warrant to search a home.
A warrant was issued after the investigation.

warrant.definition: a good reason or justification for something
examples: There is no warrant for these claims.
She had warrant to be worried.

warrant.definition: to officially approve or justify something
examples: New evidence warranted a new hearing.
The delay was not warranted by the facts.

witty.definition: quick at making clever comments or jokes
examples: She is witty and always has something funny to say.
His witty remarks made everyone laugh.

wily.definition: good at being clever and often using tricks to get what you want
examples: He was wily and negotiated hard.
A wily competitor tried to mislead them.

whinge.definition: to complain in an annoying, complaining way
examples: Stop whingeing and just do the work.
He kept whinging about the weather.

ward.definition: a section of a hospital where patients with similar needs are treated
examples: He moved to the cardiology ward.
The ward was busy all day.

ward.definition: a person under someone’s care, especially a child or someone legally protected
examples: She is the guardian of the ward.
The ward needs constant supervision.

warped.definition: twisted or bent out of shape, often by heat or force
examples: The plastic board became warped in the sun.
His idea was warped by anger.

warped.definition: to bend or change the shape of something so it no longer stays normal
examples: Cold weather can warp wood.
The metal was warped by the pressure.

wrinkled.definition: covered with wrinkles or small folds in the skin or material
examples: The wrinkled paper would not lie flat.
His forehead became wrinkled with worry.

wheedle.definition: to persuade someone gradually using gentle promises or repeated requests.
examples: She tried to wheedle an extra hour off the schedule.
He wheedled his way into the meeting.

whetstone.definition: a stone used to sharpen a knife or blade.
examples: He used a whetstone to sharpen the blade.
The whetstone was kept in the workshop.

wail.definition: to cry loudly, showing sadness or pain.
examples: She wailed after hearing the news.
The wind wails through the trees.

wail.definition: a loud cry of sadness or pain.
examples: The wail of the siren was heard for miles.
There was a wail from the crowd.

withered.definition: shriveled and dry because of lack of water or health.
examples: The withered leaves fell from the tree.
After the heatwave, the flowers looked withered.

wince.definition: to make a small movement of the face when you feel pain or unpleasant surprise.
examples: He winced when the doctor touched the wound.
She winced at the loud sound.

wiped.definition: past tense and past participle of wipe; removed something by moving a cloth or liquid over it
examples: She wiped the table clean.
He wiped the tears from his eyes.

wherewithal.definition: money or resources needed to do something
examples: They didn’t have the wherewithal to start the project.
Do you have the wherewithal to travel this week?

whatever.definition: used to say that it does not matter which thing or type you choose
examples: Take whatever book you need.
Whatever decision you make, I will support you.

whatever.definition: used to emphasize that something is not important or not worth worrying about
examples: I’ll do it however they want, whatever it takes.
Whatever, let’s just finish the task.

whatever.definition: something that does not matter which one, used when the speaker does not want to be specific
examples: You can bring whatever, as long as it fits the dress code.
Just pick whatever and we’ll start.

wack.definition: informal and slang meaning very bad, unpleasant, or not good
examples: That movie was wack.
His excuse sounded wack.

wack.definition: slang for something that is very bad or of low quality
examples: I don’t want to buy that wack.
The video was just wack.

witness.definition: a person who sees an event happen or knows about it from direct experience
examples: A witness saw the accident from across the street.
The witness gave a clear account of what happened.

witness.definition: to see something happen; to confirm that something is true based on observation
examples: I witnessed the meeting and can confirm the timeline.
The documents witnessed that the payment was made.

wiry.definition: lean and with strong, thin muscles or hair; also used for hair that feels rough and thin
examples: He has a wiry build and moves quickly.
Her wiry hair sticks out in every direction.

wraith.definition: a ghost-like figure; something that seems unreal and frightening
examples: The story describes a wraith in the old house.
He felt like a wraith after weeks without sleep.

withdraw.definition: to move back or leave a place; also to take back something such as a statement or offer
examples: Please withdraw from the building immediately.
He withdrew his offer after new information.

way.definition: a method of doing something or getting from one place to another
examples: I don’t know the way to the museum.
What’s the best way to study for the test?

way.definition: a distance or progress, especially in phrases like in a way
examples: She made progress in a way that surprised everyone.

whereupon.definition: used to say that something happens immediately after something else
examples: He apologized, whereupon the meeting continued.
The alarm sounded, whereupon everyone left the room.

writ.definition: a formal written order from a court, requiring a person to do something or appear
examples: The court issued a writ to bring the case forward.
He received a writ to appear in court.

wake.definition: the trail of disturbed water left behind by a moving boat
examples: The wake spread out behind the motorboat.
We watched the wake fade into calm water.

wake.definition: to move across water and create waves or to make someone stop sleeping and become alert
examples: The boat woke the water and made a wake.
The loud noise woke me up.

whorl.definition: a circular arrangement or pattern, especially of hair, plant growth, or fluid motion
examples: Her hair has a whorl near the crown.
The whorl in the water pulled the leaves downward.

wavy.definition: having a pattern of gentle waves or curves
examples: She wore wavy hair in loose curls.
The fence has a wavy line.

whicker.definition: to make a long, high sound that a horse makes
examples: The pony whickered as we entered the field.
I heard a whicker from the stable.

whinny.definition: to make a high sound that a horse makes
examples: The horse whinnied when it saw food.
She heard a whinny from the next stall.

whereof.definition: an older form meaning of which or about which
examples: The agreement whereof you speak is missing here.
The clause whereof the lawyer wrote was added later.
He spoke of his woe after the breakup.
The storm caused widespread woe.

woe.definition: to feel great sadness or distress
examples: She wept and woe-ed in silence.

wing.definition: a part of a building that extends from the main section
examples: The hospital has a new wing for children.
We met in the north wing.

wing.definition: a part of an aircraft that provides lift
examples: The plane banked to the left after turning.
A bird hit the wing during takeoff.

wing.definition: a side position in a sports team near the outer edge of the field
examples: He plays as a wing in the team.
The ball was passed to the wing for a quick run.

wing.definition: to move or extend as if to form a wing shape
examples: The curtain seemed to wing out as the wind came through.
Her scarf winged behind her as she ran.

wx.definition: weather information, especially as an abbreviation used in digital messages
examples: Check the wx before you go out.
The app shows hourly wx updates.

wonga.definition: money, used in informal british english
examples: He earns good wonga at the new job.
They offered him wonga for the car.

waft.definition: to move gently through the air, especially a smell or sound
examples: The smell of food wafted from the kitchen.
Her laughter wafted across the room.

waft.definition: a gentle movement through the air, often of smell
examples: A waft of perfume filled the hallway.
There was a waft of smoke from outside.

winnow.definition: to separate seeds or grain from unwanted material using air or gentle shaking
examples: They winnowed the grain after the harvest.
The wind helps winnow the chaff from the seeds.

winnow.definition: to gradually reduce a group until the best options remain
examples: The trial will winnow the applicants to the final candidates.
We need to winnow the list before the meeting.

woebegone.definition: looking or feeling very sad and unhappy
examples: He seemed woebegone after the loss.
The woebegone expression worried her.

weltschmerz.definition: a feeling of sadness or dissatisfaction with the world
examples: After the move, he felt weltschmerz for a while.
The novel explores weltschmerz and loneliness.

whim.definition: a sudden wish or desire to do something, often without planning
examples: She changed her schedule at the whim of a friend.
He bought the ticket on a whim.

wold.definition: open rolling land, often in the countryside
examples: The village sits at the edge of the wold.
We hiked across the wold on a clear day.

willowy.definition: tall, thin, and graceful like a young tree branch
examples: She is willowy and moves very lightly.
The willowy branches swayed in the wind.

wort.definition: the sweet liquid made from grains during the brewing of beer, before fermentation
examples: The wort is boiled and then cooled for fermentation.
Brewers separate wort from the grains.

wreath.definition: a ring of flowers, leaves, or other materials used for decoration or remembrance
examples: They placed a wreath at the memorial.
A wreath hung on the front door.

wreath.definition: to surround with something, especially in a circle
examples: Vines wreath the fence in summer.
Smoke wreaths around the room.

wee.definition: very small, in amount or size
examples: I’ll take a wee bit of sugar.
She moved a wee chair into the corner.

Add a wee of salt.

waspish.definition: quick to criticize or reply in an annoying, sharp way
examples: Her waspish tone made everyone tense.
He became waspish when the question was repeated.

weft.definition: the threads that run across fabric, perpendicular to the warp
examples: The weft holds the pattern together.
Weft threads were visible on the surface.

wyrd.definition: fate or destiny, especially in older literature and folklore
examples: In the legend, the wyrd decided their outcome.
The story treats wyrd as unstoppable.

weal.definition: well-being or welfare, especially for a group of people
examples: The plan supports the weal of the community.
They acted for the weal of all citizens.

weal.definition: a place or village of a certain kind, in old or dialect use
examples: The historical map shows a small weal near the river.

wally.definition: a foolish or silly person, used informally
examples: He’s such a wally for forgetting his keys.
